html:
The Tukular Caliphate was the Islamic empire founded by the scholar and warrior Umar Tall on the upper Niger and Senegal rivers, in what is now Mali, from 1852 to 1893. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. Its name comes from the Toucouleur people of Futa Toro, who made up much of its army.

Umar was a leader of the Tijaniyya Sufi order who had made the pilgrimage to Mecca. He launched his jihad in 1852. Blocked by the French at Medine in 1857, he turned east. He conquered the Bambara kingdoms of Kaarta in 1855 and Segou in 1861, and in 1862 the Fula state of Massina, though it was already Muslim. Massina rebelled, and Umar died in 1864 in the cliffs near Bandiagara.

His son Ahmadu ruled from Segou, while relatives held other provinces. The French, advancing from Senegal, took Segou in 1890 and the last strongholds by 1893, and the land became part of French West Africa.
